sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is really being decided, and which numbers and dates frame it?
criteria: Separates the 90-day risk control, the platform and the operating model into distinct decisions
Derives next year's model spend with compounding growth ($25.1M), not 12 × $1.5M
Identifies the 36 infrastructure roles (22 needed) as the duplication, not all 150 staff
States the autos launch and the 90-day deadline as the clash that shapes the plan

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers the CEO, audit committee, CFO, CTO and at least two unit presidents, each with a distinct want
Says what the CTO gets when their proposal is not adopted
Includes the infrastructure staff who move and what they are told
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real operating models, and how does each fare on people, money and risk?
criteria: Includes the status quo, the CTO's full centralization and at least one hybrid
Prices extra attrition from HR's data for each option
Shows how the 90-day control is met under each option
Compares options on one table over the same 3-year horizon

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would change it?
criteria: Makes one clear recommendation, including where the platform reports
Decouples the risk control from the reorg so the deadline doesn't depend on moving people
Says which moves are reversible and which are not
Gives a dated revisit with measurable triggers

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: Where do the savings come from, and what does each option cost over three years?
criteria: Derives the routing and caching saving from list prices and the audit's shares (about 38%)
Phases savings by when each unit reaches the gateway, autos last
Separates new spend and attrition cost from payroll already paid
Labels assumptions such as flat spend after month 12 and ignored cache writes

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who decides what between the platform and the business units, and who pays?
criteria: Gives a decision-rights table between platform and units
Names one accountable owner for AI risk
States a funding model (central platform, model spend billed to units at cost)
Gives the platform a service target so units don't route around it

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens by day 90, by the autos launch and after it?
criteria: Has a control covering every unit, autos included, before day 90
Moves no autos staff before the month-5 launch
Tells movers one to one before any announcement
Includes the month-12 revisit as a milestone

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong with the reorg and the controls, and what manages it?
criteria: Quantifies expected departures among moved staff
Puts the vendor control in the network and gateway, not only in policy
Gates routing changes on each use case's evals
Addresses vendor concentration after contracts are consolidated

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the new model works, and what would show harm?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Guards platform savings with unit velocity
Tracks gateway coverage against the day-90 and month-7 targets
Tracks moved-staff attrition against HR's 24%

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, in what order and how often?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least five audiences
Sequences the news: movers first, then presidents, then the wider organization
Gives the audit committee a reporting cadence until the inquiry closes
Tells infrastructure staff plainly that nobody is being cut
